tagline: Pioneering electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft for urban air mobility
hero_kpi_rationale: The company is fully focused on eVTOL technological development and regulatory certification, making R&D investments critical for its survival and future leadership in urban air mobility.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Headcount is concentrated in engineering and aeronautical development, reflecting a lean organizational model centered on aerospace engineering expertise. The combined team has previously certified and supported the development of over 30 aircraft and propulsion systems.
kpis.signal: Highly skilled workforce in aerospace and aeronautical engineering.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from the company's activities.
kpis.description: No revenue has been generated from the design, development, manufacturing, engineering, sale, or distribution of aircraft during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. The company is fully funded by equity investments and grants.
kpis.signal: Pre-revenue company in development and certification phase.

kpis.name: Cash and cash equivalents
kpis.explanation: Available liquidity to fund operations and development.
kpis.description: Cash is essential to fund development, flight testing, regulatory certification by the CAA and EASA, and commercialization preparations. Equity and debt financing are crucial for executing the company's strategy.
kpis.signal: Cash is critical to fund development through certification and commercialization.

kpis.name: Flight test progress
kpis.explanation: Milestones achieved in the eVTOL prototype flight test program.
kpis.description: The second prototype advanced from Phase 2 (piloted hover flights, December 2024) to Phase 3 (wing-borne flight, May 2025), and now to Phase 4 (piloted transition, November 2025). A third fully assembled identical prototype completed in December 2025 will double flight test capacity and accelerate design validation.
kpis.signal: Second eVTOL prototype to accelerate development and testing.

kpis.name: Regulatory certification status
kpis.explanation: Progress toward obtaining CAA and EASA certification.
kpis.description: The CAA granted an eVTOL DOA in March 2023, extended in July 2024, authorizing sign-off of compliance on aeronautical engineering. The DOA was maintained following a 24-month audit in 2025. The CAA and EASA have agreed to collaborate on certification with common standards. The UK eVTOL Delivery Model (2025) establishes a framework for commercial eVTOL operations by end-2028.
kpis.signal: Design Organization Approval (DOA) maintained and extended; UK eVTOL regulatory framework in place.

kpis.name: eVTOL product portfolio
kpis.explanation: Aircraft variants under development: fully electric and hybrid-electric.
kpis.description: Valo is the 100% fully electric eVTOL aircraft, designed to carry one pilot and up to six passengers, up to 100 miles, at 150 mph cruise speed. A complementary hybrid-electric aircraft, announced in May 2025, offers 1,100 kg payload and 1,000+ miles range, enabling defense, logistics, and air ambulance applications.
kpis.signal: Portfolio expansion to address multiple use cases (civil, defense, logistics, air ambulance).

risks.title: Absence of commercial aircraft production and certification
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk mentioned in forward-looking statements. Maximum intensity: the company has never produced a non-prototype aircraft or sold any unit. Stable trend but critical for business viability. Very high weight for an aerospace manufacturer.

risks.title: Critical dependence on key suppliers and partners
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited in forward-looking statements as a major risk. Direct language: 'dependence on our partners and suppliers'. Stable but structural trend. High weight for a manufacturing startup without established vertical integration.

risks.title: Technological and aircraft performance risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned: 'aircraft may not perform at the level we expect and may potentially have defects'. Strong uncertainty language. Stable but inherent to aerospace R&D. Critical weight for a manufacturer of new aircraft types.

risks.title: Sector-wide accidents or incidents affecting reputation
risks.score_rationale: Explicit risk in forward-looking statements: 'accidents or incidents involving eVTOL...could harm our business'. Direct impact language. Stable trend but increasing with the emergence of the AAM sector. High weight for a nascent industry sensitive to incidents.

risks.title: Volatility of pre-orders and refund conditions
risks.score_rationale: Specific risk cited: 'All pre-orders...are conditional and may be terminated...any pre-delivery payments may be fully refundable'. Language indicating uncertainty around order book. Stable but structural trend. High weight for a revenue-less startup.

risks.title: Hybrid-electric development risks and technological complexity
risks.score_rationale: Specifically mentioned: 'Development...of hybrid-electric variant...subject to significant risks, including technological, regulatory and operational challenges'. Multidimensional uncertainty language. Stable but increasing with product evolution. High weight for product strategy.

risks.title: Rapid growth and operational management risks
risks.score_rationale: Cited in forward-looking statements: 'business has developed rapidly...failure to manage that growth effectively could harm'. Moderate language but acknowledges challenges. Stable trend. Medium weight for a scaling startup.

risks.title: Dependence on management team and specialized talent
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned: 'dependence on recruiting and retaining our senior management team and other highly skilled personnel'. Direct language. Stable but structural for an aerospace startup. Medium weight for a young company.
